udt_struct_v0.doc:
Everything the fill needs, staged by [`InterestFlash::a`] and consumed by
[`InterestFlash::exec_op`] in the same transaction.

The loaned asset is **not** in here: `exec_op` receives it from Blend and
uses it as the join asset, the lot's principal asset and the repay asset, so
there is no way for those three to disagree.
udt_struct_v0.name: Plan

fields.doc: The Blend V2 backstop \xe2\x80\x94 the auction's `user` key, and the address that\npulls the bid inside `donate`.
fields.name: backstop

fields.doc: The Comet BLND:USDC pool. A Comet pool *is* its own LP token, so this\naddress is both the join target and the bid asset.
fields.name: comet

fields.doc: The Blend pool the flash loan comes from. Declared so a same-pool plan\nfails with a named error instead of the host's bare `InvalidAction`.
fields.name: loan_pool

fields.doc: Refuse if the runtime-scaled bid exceeds this many LP. A cap on how much\nof the loan the join may consume, priced off-chain against the lot.
fields.name: max_bid_lp

fields.doc:
Hard ceiling on the loaned asset the join may spend. Passed to Comet as
`max_amount_in`, which is also the amount of the nested approve Comet
grants itself \xe2\x80\x94 so this value, and not a runtime one, is what the
authorization has to name.
fields.name: max_usdc_in

fields.doc:
Loaned-asset balance this contract must hold before handing back.

Set it to **loan principal + 1 stroop at minimum**. Blend converts the
borrow to d-tokens with a ceiling and back to underlying with a ceiling,
so the amount `handle_transfer_with_allowance` pulls is normally one
stroop above the principal \xe2\x80\x94 measured live on mainnet 2026-08-24, where
a 250.0000000 USDC loan was repaid at 250.0000001. That double-ceiling
*is* the "protocol fee is rounding dust" figure, observed rather than
inferred. Below `min_repay` the transaction reverts here rather than at
Blend's repay `transfer_from`.
fields.name: min_repay

fields.doc: The Blend pool the auction lives on. Must differ from `loan_pool`.
fields.name: pool

fields.doc: EURC \xe2\x86\x92 loaned-asset conversion. Empty for a USDC-only lot.
fields.name: swaps

cases.doc: The plan borrows from the very pool whose auction it fills. The Soroban\nhost would reject that re-entry anyway (`Context/InvalidAction`); this\nturns it into something greppable.
cases.name: SamePoolReentrancy

cases.doc: A non-positive cap, or a fraction above 100 %.
cases.name: BadParams

cases.doc: The auction has no bid in the backstop token, or has not started\n(`ledger < auction.block`).
cases.name: NoAuction

cases.doc: The scaled bid is above `max_bid_lp` \xe2\x80\x94 the fill would cost more than it\nwas priced at. Reverts fee-only.
cases.name: BidAboveCap

cases.doc: The join pulled more of the loaned asset than `max_usdc_in`.
cases.name: SpendCapExceeded

cases.doc: LP is still held after the fill. `dep_lp_tokn_amt_out_get_tokn_in` mints\nexactly the bid and `donate` takes exactly the bid, so any residual\nmeans one of those two contracts did not behave as read.
cases.name: LpResidual

cases.doc: The lot (plus whatever the swaps converted) does not cover `min_repay`.\nEverything rolls back \xe2\x80\x94 the loan, the join and the fill.
cases.name: InsufficientRepay

cases.doc:
`exec_op` was driven by something other than the orchestrator this
contract was constructed against. Only the pinned orchestrator may
receive the swept balance \xe2\x80\x94 see the `exec_op` note. This is the fix for
the "drainable by anyone" defect.
cases.name: UnexpectedCaller

cases.doc:
The join did not mint exactly the bid.

`dep_lp_tokn_amt_out_get_tokn_in` is **exact-LP-out**: it is documented
to mint precisely `pool_amount_out` and its own `ErrLimitIn` bounds what
it charges. So the LP delta this contract measures on its own balance is
an *independent* expectation, and a disagreement means the Comet pool did
not behave the way its source reads.

This matters because the backstop token is Comet BLND:USDC
`CAS3FL6T\xe2\x80\xa6`, whose deployed wasm carries a live, unpatched
balance-desync defect: `execute_swap_exact_amount_in` never checks
`token_in != token_out`, and a self-swap writes `in_record` then
`out_record` into the same map key, so the last write wins and the
recorded reserve silently drifts below the tokens actually held (that
pool was drained of 717,519 USDC on 2026-08-25 and the wasm is
unchanged). Every quote taken from it may therefore be computed off
corrupted state.

The spend ceiling already bounds what a corrupted quote can cost us;
this bounds what it can *deliver*, and it fires
cases.name: LpMintMismatch

udt_struct_v0.doc:
Blend's `AuctionData`, as returned by `pool.get_auction(auction_type, user)`
(`pool/src/auctions/auction.rs`). A `#[contracttype]` struct is encoded as a
symbol-keyed map, so field order here is irrelevant to the wire format \xe2\x80\x94
only the names and types matter.
udt_struct_v0.name: AuctionData

fields.doc: Assets spent by the filler. For an interest auction: exactly one entry,\nkeyed by the backstop token (the Comet BLND:USDC LP).
fields.name: bid

fields.doc: The ledger the auction became fillable at.
fields.name: block

fields.doc: Assets paid to the filler \xe2\x80\x94 the pool's accrued interest, USDC and\nsometimes EURC.
fields.name: lot

function_v0.doc:
Stage the plan in temporary storage.

The two-argument shape is the deployed orchestrator's ABI: it calls
`receiver.a(b, h)` with the two opaque `Val`s it was handed. `_h` is
Parallax's sub-auth list, which this contract does not use \xe2\x80\x94 its
authorizations are derived on-chain, not supplied.

Permissionless, like Parallax v5's `a`. Nothing here moves money, the
entry is temporary, and `exec_op` deletes it before doing anything \xe2\x80\x94
and both calls live inside the orchestrator's single invocation, so no
other transaction can interleave with them.
function_v0.name: a

function_v0.doc:
Blend flash-loan callback: buy the bid with the borrowed asset, win the
auction, convert the non-principal side of the lot, hand everything to
`caller`.

* `caller` \xe2\x80\x94 the `from` of `pool.flash_loan`, i.e. the orchestrator. It
owes the pool the repayment and holds the allowance to satisfy it, so
this is where the proceeds must go. It is **verified** against the
pinned orchestrator, not trusted: see the check at the top of the body.
* `token_addr` \xe2\x80\x94 the loaned asset. Used as the join asset, the lot's
principal asset and the repay asset.
* `c` / `d` \xe2\x80\x94 borrowed amount and fee. `c + d` is the real repayment
obligation Blend enforces a frame later; the hand-back must clear it
(and `Plan.min_repay`, the priced floor). The whole balance still goes
back \xe2\x80\x94 Blend's fee is rounding dust and any surplus is profit \xe2\x80\x94 but the
loan is no longer discarded: it is the structural lower bound.

Panics \xe2\x80\x94 reverting the loan with it \xe2\x80\x94 on any bound violation, and
propagates Comet's and Blend's panics untouched. A lost ra
function_v0.name: exec_op

function_v0.doc:
Pin the orchestrator at deploy time. This is the only persistent state
the contract ever holds and there is no setter, so the address is
immutable for the life of the deployment \xe2\x80\x94 the same discipline the
orchestrator itself uses for its payout address.

`exec_op` will hand the swept balance to exactly this address and refuse
to run for any other `caller`. In production it is the deployed
orchestrator `CA4I5TPQ\xe2\x80\xa6`.
